⚠️ Thousands of wallets in the Cardano ecosystem may be at risk

SecondFi (formerly Yoroi) has reportedly suffered a security incident related to wallet generation, potentially exposing users' private keys.

What we know so far:

🔴 Around 16 million ADA ($2.4M) has already been stolen from 374 wallets.
🔴 The platform has suspended its services, entered maintenance mode, and promised to compensate affected users.
🔴 Large transfers totaling 129 million ADA, initially suspected to be theft, were actually executed by SecondFi itself to secure user funds.
🔴 If the issue is indeed caused by predictable private key generation, all wallets created through the vulnerable version of the app could remain at risk.

❗️Most importantly, the team is advising users NOT to move funds to new wallets and NOT to import their seed phrases into other applications. According to the developers, the risk appears to arise during transaction signing itself.

For now, Cardano users should closely follow official updates and avoid taking rushed actions that could make the situation worse. 👀

📌 Bonding Curves: How Token Prices Move With Every Buy and Sell

Main Points
⏺ Bonding curves define a token’s price as a math function of supply
⏺ Every buy pushes the price up along the curve; every sell pushes it down
⏺ This post explains why bonding curves are popular for launches and micro-caps

1️⃣ Core Concept — instead of an order book, a smart contract sets the price based on how many tokens are already minted or held.
2️⃣ Automatic Pricing — early buyers get cheaper tokens; as demand increases, the curve raises the price automatically.
3️⃣ Liquidity Built-In — the contract always stands ready to buy back tokens along the same curve, so there’s no traditional LP needed.
4️⃣ Design Choices — steeper curves pump price faster but are more volatile; flatter curves are smoother but less “explosive.”
5️⃣ Risks — thin real liquidity, manipulation, and the fact that math-driven pricing doesn’t guarantee real fundamental value.

Final Thoughts

Bonding curves turn token price into a formula instead of a market guess — transparent, but still only as meaningful as the demand behind it.

Former Ethereum Foundation developer Trent Van Epps warns that Ethereum could face a funding crisis within the next 3–9 months 

For years, the Ethereum Foundation has followed a “subtraction” strategy—gradually reducing its influence so the network can thrive independently. However, EF still remains a key pillar of legitimacy through its brand, ties to Vitalik Buterin, developer events, and ecosystem coordination.

The bigger issue is funding. After spending much of its ETH reserves on ecosystem growth, EF plans to cut annual spending from 15% to 5% by 2030. Meanwhile, its 4-year Client Incentive Program ended in April 2026 with no replacement announced.

Maintaining client teams, research, and protocol coordination costs around $30M per year. Without a sustainable funding model, Ethereum risks losing experienced developers and slowing progress on scaling, quantum-resistance research, and core network maintenance.

Ethereum’s biggest challenge may not be technology—it may be funding the people building it.

“The ten horns which you saw are ten kings who have received no kingdom as yet, but they receive authority for one hour as kings with the beast. These are of one mind, and they will give their power and authority to the beast.”
(Revelation 17:12-13 NKJV)

These ten kings could represent:

▪️Ten individual nations

▪️Ten regional blocs

▪️Ten leaders representing larger coalitions

▪️A reorganized global governance structure that does not presently exist

One thing, however, remains certain. While we should pray for our countries and for those who lead them (1 Timothy 2:1-2), we must never forget the temporary nature of both. Our greatest concern should be to ensure that our names are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life (Revelation 21:27).

As the prophet Daniel declared:

“And in the days of these kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed; and the kingdom shall not be left to other people; it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever.”
(Daniel 2:44 NKJV)

Being removed from this evil world into the everlasting presence of our beloved Messiah - and ultimately to our eternal residence in the New Jerusalem, according to His promise - is our blessed hope!

“Let not your heart be troubled; you believe in God, believe also in Me. In My Father’s house are many mansions; if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and receive you to Myself; that where I am, there you may be also.”
(John 14:1-3 NKJV)

Hormuz 2.0: The Strait Got Nationalized

The Iranian delegation didn’t fly home from Switzerland — they went straight to Muscat to rewrite the rules of one of the world’s most important arteries. 

Meeting Sultan Haitham, Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi blessed a new deal where only two states get a say over the Strait of Hormuz: the Islamic Republic of Iran and Oman. 

The message to Washington, Brussels and the oil majors is simple: the colonial era of “international management” is over; traffic now passes through a joint Iranian–Omani spreadsheet.

A joint committee was announced, plus a mutual declaration: any future arrangement must “fully respect the sovereignty and sovereign rights” of both countries, while keeping Hormuz formally “safe and open” for international shipping. 

Oman’s foreign minister promises “free and safe passage without fees,” which sounds wonderfully liberal — right up until you remember who now decides what counts as “safe,” and how quickly a “fee” can be renamed a “service.” It’s not a toll if the tollbooth calls itself a security agency.

Over in Washington, Trump plays his own numbers game. He says he agreed to keep the strait “open” with no blockade, but insists US naval assets are staying put “just in case,” and boasts that 19 million barrels of oil passed through Hormuz “yesterday — an all‑time record.” 

Tehran’s media immediately calls that fiction, saying only a limited number of ships got permits and that volumes fluctuate daily. 

Tanker‑tracking platforms add a third version: about 36 million barrels exported since June 15, based on actual ship movements rather than White House brag sheets or IRGC spin.

Hovering over all of it is Ghalibaf’s line: “Everyone must understand that the management of the Strait of Hormuz will never return to what it was before the war.” 

That’s the real story. Hormuz is no longer a neutral corridor policed by anonymous “international forces”; it’s a lever openly claimed by one sanctioned state and its quiet Gulf neighbour, with American tankers and warships reduced to guests in a choke point they used to treat as their own maritime hallway. 

Cheap oil, “free passage,” global stability — all now depend on a strait whose new owners have every incentive to keep the world guessing about which number is real.

🔔 Ripple targets $1B revenue run rate without counting XRP holdings 

❗️ According to posts shared by CoinMarketCap and crypto-focused accounts on X, Ripple expects to end 2026 with a $1 billion revenue run rate. The figure does not include XRP held on Ripple’s balance sheet. That detail matters because Ripple has long faced public debate over the link between its business and XRP. Garlinghouse’s target frames the company as a fintech infrastructure provider that aims to earn money from products, clients, and services, not from token holdings or sales.

🌐 The deal also supports Ripple USD, known as RLUSD. Ripple has promoted the stablecoin for enterprise settlement and collateral use. Recently, crypto news reported that Ripple is also adding RLUSD to new payment tools, including services tied to AI agents and machine payments on the XRP Ledger. Company materials point to custody, treasury management, and liquidity services as core offerings. These products target banks and firms that need faster settlement, account control, and access to digital assets through regulated processes, rather than retail trading.
